events.title: Surprise Classmate
events.description: You walk into your elective lecture and realize Hiyori is already seated. Apparently she needed science credits and picked the same module. She looks up, blinks, and says 'oh. it's you.'
events.player_action_prompt: You're now in the same lecture. What do you do?

affection_outcomes.high: Offer to share notes or sit nearby without making it weird
affection_outcomes.mid: Acknowledge her and focus on the lecture
affection_outcomes.low: Make a big deal of it or ignore her completely

events.title: Coincidence [Location]
events.description: You run into Hiyori together with Shiori while [activity]. The encounter lasts longer than any of you planned.

location_options: on the MRT heading to Clementi
at the bus stop outside UTown
at a bubble tea place near Clementi Mall

events.player_action_prompt: The three of you end up talking for a while. What do you talk to Hiyori about?

affection_outcomes.high: Ask about something she's interested in and actually engage with her answer
affection_outcomes.mid: Keep it light and friendly
affection_outcomes.low: Dominate the conversation or barely acknowledge her

events.title: Just the Two of You
events.description: You run into Hiyori alone — no Shiori, no buffer. She's at [location] by herself. She notices you first.

location_options: the mixed rice stall near Science block
the UTown lawn with her laptop
a convenience store near her hostel at 10pm
a bus stop in light rain

events.player_action_prompt: She's alone. It's just you two. What do you say?

affection_outcomes.high: Join her naturally, ask something genuine, don't overstay
affection_outcomes.mid: Say hi, chat briefly, leave when it feels right
affection_outcomes.low: Make it awkward, overstay, or don't say anything at all

events.title: Orientation Planning Committee
events.description: You've both somehow ended up on the planning committee for a faculty orientation event. You'll be working together across several meetings over the next week.
events.player_action_prompt: First committee meeting. You're assigned to the same sub-team as Hiyori. How do you approach working with her?

affection_outcomes.high: Pull your weight, be organized, let her lead where she wants to
affection_outcomes.mid: Do your part, be pleasant
affection_outcomes.low: Slack off, be disorganized, or try too hard to impress

events.notes: Active event. Sub-events fire preferentially over the 7-day window; unrelated events can still occur but less frequently.

sub_events.description: The committee splits into pairs to scout venues. You end up paired with Hiyori, walking between three possible faculty halls with a clipboard neither of you asked for.
sub_events.player_action_prompt: It's just the two of you scouting venues for an hour. What do you talk about between checklist items?

affection_outcomes.high: Balance the task with genuine conversation, let silences be comfortable rather than awkward
affection_outcomes.mid: Stick mostly to the task, light small talk
affection_outcomes.low: Either ignore her or talk over the task entirely

sub_events.description: A planning meeting runs late — everyone else trickles out, but you and Hiyori stay behind finishing the budget sheet.
sub_events.player_action_prompt: It's just the two of you finishing up. The room is quieter than usual. What do you do?

affection_outcomes.high: Work efficiently together, then let one small personal question slip in naturally
affection_outcomes.mid: Finish the task, keep things professional
affection_outcomes.low: Rush off immediately or make the moment feel forced

sub_events.description: You and Hiyori disagree on how to run one of the orientation activities. Nothing dramatic, but the rest of the committee is watching how it plays out.
sub_events.player_action_prompt: You two see this differently. How do you handle the disagreement?

affection_outcomes.high: Hear her out fully, find a compromise, don't need to be right
affection_outcomes.mid: Concede quickly just to avoid conflict
affection_outcomes.low: Push your view and dismiss hers in front of others

sub_events.description: Another committee work block — venue lists, budget sheets, someone's laptop dying. Hiyori's at the same table, half-listening to the same argument you are.
sub_events.player_action_prompt: It's slow, unglamorous committee work and you're both stuck in it. How do you spend the time?

affection_outcomes.high: Make the tedious work bearable — share the load, keep the mood light without slacking
affection_outcomes.mid: Do your own portion and let her do hers
affection_outcomes.low: Coast and let her pick up the slack, or complain the whole way through

sub_events.description: The committee group chat is still going at night — last-minute changes, someone volunteering someone else. Hiyori's typing too.
sub_events.player_action_prompt: The chat's a mess and something needs sorting before tomorrow. What do you do?

affection_outcomes.high: Quietly sort the thing out and back her up when she's talked over
affection_outcomes.mid: Reply when directly asked, otherwise stay out of it
affection_outcomes.low: Add to the noise or dump the problem on her

events.title: Night of the Cultural Production Show
events.description: NUS Cultural Night. Hiyori is in the main cast — she's been rehearsing for weeks. You somehow ended up volunteering for backstage crew (lights/props). You'll see a side of her most people don't see: nervous, focused, completely in it.
events.player_action_prompt: You're backstage before the show. She's going over her lines quietly by herself. Do you say anything?

affection_outcomes.high: Say something genuine and low-pressure — not 'you'll be amazing' but something that shows you see her
affection_outcomes.mid: Wish her luck simply
affection_outcomes.low: Say something performatively supportive or say nothing

sub_events.description: Final dress rehearsal. Hiyori flubs a line twice and looks visibly frustrated with herself during the break.
sub_events.player_action_prompt: She's frustrated and trying to hide it. What do you do?

affection_outcomes.high: Say something light to break the tension without dismissing how she feels
affection_outcomes.mid: Give her space, don't say much
affection_outcomes.low: Point out the mistake or make it a bigger deal than it is

sub_events.description: After the show, backstage. She comes offstage still buzzing, adrenaline high, makeup slightly smudged from the lights.
sub_events.player_action_prompt: She's still riding the high of the performance. This is a key moment. What do you say?

affection_outcomes.high: Match her energy, be specific about what you actually noticed during the show
affection_outcomes.mid: Congratulate her simply
affection_outcomes.low: Be distracted, generic, or make it about your own night backstage

sub_events.description: Setup and run-throughs all day — props in the wrong place, cues missed, everyone slightly on edge. Hiyori's somewhere in the middle of it.
sub_events.player_action_prompt: There's more to do than time to do it and she's clearly stretched. What do you do?

affection_outcomes.high: Take something off her plate without being asked or making it a thing
affection_outcomes.mid: Handle your own assigned bits
affection_outcomes.low: Add to her stress or hover without actually helping

sub_events.description: Practice running late again. The hall's mostly empty, a few people still going over the same eight bars.
sub_events.player_action_prompt: It's late and she's still here working on it. How do you handle the moment?

affection_outcomes.high: Stay without making a production of staying — company, not pressure
affection_outcomes.mid: Say goodnight and head off
affection_outcomes.low: Push her to call it a night in a way that reads as dismissive of the work

events.title: The Group Project From Hell
events.description: You and Hiyori somehow get assigned to the same interdisciplinary group project — a mandatory module requirement pairing CS and Life Sciences students. Two other groupmates are functionally useless. It's you two carrying it for the week.
events.player_action_prompt: First group meeting makes it clear it's going to be mostly you and Hiyori doing the actual work. How do you approach this?

affection_outcomes.high: Suggest splitting work fairly and check in with her without micromanaging
affection_outcomes.mid: Go along with whatever she suggests
affection_outcomes.low: Try to offload work onto her or complain about the other groupmates to her

events.notes: Active event. Good vehicle for low-stakes daily proximity without romantic pressure.

sub_events.description: You're both stuck on the same part of the project at 11pm and end up on a call troubleshooting it together.
sub_events.player_action_prompt: It's late and you're both tired but making progress. What's the vibe on the call?

affection_outcomes.high: Stay focused but let some humor and casual conversation in
affection_outcomes.mid: Keep it strictly about the project
affection_outcomes.low: Get irritable or short with her over the frustration

sub_events.description: Presentation day. The two useless groupmates barely show up prepared. You and Hiyori end up covering for them on the spot.
sub_events.player_action_prompt: You have to improvise together in front of the class. How do you handle it?

affection_outcomes.high: Back her up smoothly, make her look good, don't take more credit than you deserve
affection_outcomes.mid: Get through it functionally
affection_outcomes.low: Panic and leave her to cover for both of you

sub_events.description: Another working session on the project. The other two groupmates are 'busy' again, so it's the same two of you and a half-finished slide deck.
sub_events.player_action_prompt: You're carrying this together and there's a lot left. How do you approach the session?

affection_outcomes.high: Split things sensibly, take the part she'd rather not do, keep it collaborative
affection_outcomes.mid: Work through your own section quietly
affection_outcomes.low: Micromanage her half or grumble about the groupmates the whole time

sub_events.description: Evening, project files open, messages going back and forth about a section neither of you likes.
sub_events.player_action_prompt: Neither of you is stopping any time soon. What's the tone?

affection_outcomes.high: Keep it human — let some humor in, notice when she needs a break
affection_outcomes.mid: Stay strictly on task
affection_outcomes.low: Get short with her because you're tired

events.title: You Did WHAT
events.description: While looking through Shiori's following list to find Hiyori's Instagram, you accidentally hit follow on her profile. Or worse — while in your contacts looking at Hiyori's number Shiori gave you, you accidentally call her. One ring. You hang up. Your phone rings back immediately.

incident_options: accidentally followed her Instagram while trying to look at her profile
accidentally liked a photo from 47 weeks ago while scrolling
accidentally called her when her number was open on your screen
accidentally sent a half-typed message you were writing to Shiori to Hiyori instead

events.player_action_prompt: Oh no. It happened. What do you do?

affection_outcomes.high: Own it immediately with a self-deprecating honest message — she will respect the honesty
affection_outcomes.mid: Pretend it didn't happen and hope she does the same
affection_outcomes.low: Send a panicked weird message that makes it worse

events.notes: This event has high entertainment value and can actually INCREASE affection significantly if handled well — it breaks the ice in an unexpected way.

events.title: 2AM at the Library
events.description: Finals season. You're at the 24-hour library on Level 5 at 2am, barely functional, surrounded by your laptop and cold coffee. You look up and Hiyori is three tables away, handwriting notes with a highlighter in her mouth, equally destroyed.
events.player_action_prompt: You make eye contact. The universal language of exam suffering. What do you do?

affection_outcomes.high: Go over quietly, exchange a few exhausted words, maybe offer to grab drinks from the vending machine
affection_outcomes.mid: Wave and smile, leave it at that
affection_outcomes.low: Ignore it or say something annoying about her major vs yours

events.title: Her Story
events.description: Hiyori posts a vague sad story on Instagram at 11pm — just a grey background and a song lyric. No caption. You see it. You don't know if you should say something.
events.player_action_prompt: You see the story. What do you do?

affection_outcomes.high: Send a casual, non-pushy message — 'hey, you okay?' Nothing more. Give her room.
affection_outcomes.mid: React to the story with an emoji and leave it
affection_outcomes.low: Don't respond, or send something overwhelming and over-the-top

events.title: And Then There Were Two
events.description: A group outing that Shiori organized. One by one, people drop out with excuses — last minute assignment, sick, family thing. By the time you're at the meeting point, it's just you and Hiyori.

location_options: a weekend market at Pasir Pagar

events.player_action_prompt: It's just you and her. She looks at you and says 'well... do you still want to go?' What do you say?

affection_outcomes.high: Say yes without making it a big deal — treat it like any other hangout and let it be what it is
affection_outcomes.mid: Agree but seem slightly awkward about it
affection_outcomes.low: Make it weird or suggest cancelling

events.title: Can I Get Your Notes?
events.description: You're in the same module now. Hiyori missed a lecture for her tutoring commitment and texts you (through Shiori's suggestion) asking if you have notes she could borrow. This turns into a study session.
events.player_action_prompt: You're now studying together in the library. What's the vibe you go for?

affection_outcomes.high: Focused but naturally conversational — study first, talk when it happens organically
affection_outcomes.mid: Keep it academic and friendly
affection_outcomes.low: Use it as an excuse to not actually study or make her feel like she owes you

events.title: You Hear Something
events.description: You're near the Science canteen when you overhear — or Shiori tells you — that someone else asked Hiyori out. She apparently said she needed to think about it.
events.player_action_prompt: You just found out someone else is interested in her and she hasn't said no. What do you do with this information?

affection_outcomes.high: Don't panic. Stay consistent. Let your presence speak — don't suddenly over-pursue or act possessive.
affection_outcomes.mid: Sit on it and wait
affection_outcomes.low: Act weird around her, become distant, or bring it up to her directly in an awkward way

events.notes: If affection is already high (60+) when this event triggers, Hiyori will turn the other person down on her own. Player doesn't know this.

events.title: It's Raining
events.description: Classic. It starts raining out of nowhere while you're both outside — no umbrella. You have one. She doesn't.
events.player_action_prompt: It's raining. You have an umbrella. She's about to make a run for it. What do you do?

affection_outcomes.high: Offer without making it theatrical. Walk with her. Don't make it a moment.
affection_outcomes.mid: Offer and let her decide
affection_outcomes.low: Don't offer, or make such a big deal of offering that it becomes weird

events.title: Late Night From Yuki
events.description: It's 11:30pm. You get a text from Yuki. 'Hey. Are you awake?' — she says it's about something random. It isn't really.
events.player_action_prompt: Yuki texted you late at night. What do you reply?

affection_outcomes.high_yuki: Reply warmly, ask what's up, stay in the conversation — Yuki's hidden affection increases
affection_outcomes.mid: Reply briefly and keep it short
affection_outcomes.low_yuki: Leave it on read or give a one-word reply

events.notes: This event is one of several that contributes to Yuki's hidden affection meter. Player does not know this meter exists.

events.title: Yuki Needs a Favor
events.description: Yuki texts asking if you can help her make sense of a basic statistics concept for an econs module — something you covered in a CS module last year. It's a flimsy excuse and you both sort of know it.
events.player_action_prompt: Yuki asked for your help with something she probably could've figured out herself. What do you do?

affection_outcomes.high_yuki: Actually help properly and ask her how her other modules are going too
affection_outcomes.mid: Help quickly and move on
affection_outcomes.low_yuki: Brush her off or make her feel like she's wasting your time

events.notes: Contributes to Yuki's hidden affection meter.

events.title: Just the Three of Us. Wait, Two.
events.description: Yuki invites you to dinner, framing it as a group thing with Shiori. Shiori cancels last minute citing an assignment. Yuki doesn't seem surprised.
events.player_action_prompt: It's just you and Yuki at dinner now. What's the conversation like?

affection_outcomes.high_yuki: Be genuinely present, ask about her rather than defaulting to talking about Hiyori
affection_outcomes.mid: Keep it casual and friendly
affection_outcomes.low_yuki: Spend the dinner talking mostly about Hiyori

events.notes: A meaningful contributor to Yuki's hidden affection meter — this event tests whether the player treats Yuki as her own person.

events.title: She's Not Replying
events.description: Hiyori hasn't replied to the group chat all day, which is unusual for her. Shiori mentions she's been sick in her hostel room since yesterday.
events.player_action_prompt: You know she's sick and alone in her hostel room. What do you do, if anything?

affection_outcomes.high: Check in directly, offer to drop off something practical (soup, medicine) without making it a big gesture
affection_outcomes.mid: Send a text wishing her well
affection_outcomes.low: Don't do anything or wait for someone else to handle it

events.title: Come Ride With Us
events.description: Hiyori mentions, almost as an afterthought, that her cycling club is doing an easy beginner-friendly route this Saturday and 'anyone can join if they want.' She doesn't quite look at you when she says it.
events.player_action_prompt: It sounded like an offer, even if she didn't frame it as one directed at you. What do you do?

affection_outcomes.high: Say yes plainly, show up prepared, don't make a big deal of the invitation
affection_outcomes.mid: Say maybe and leave it uncertain
affection_outcomes.low: Decline dismissively or make a joke that undercuts the invitation

events.title: Something She Mentioned
events.description: Hiyori mentions, very casually, that she applied for an overseas exchange program 'on a whim' and probably won't get in. She changes the subject quickly after.
events.player_action_prompt: She brought it up and then moved past it fast. Do you follow up?

affection_outcomes.high: Ask one genuine follow-up question, then let her steer if she wants to talk more or not
affection_outcomes.mid: Acknowledge it lightly and move on with her
affection_outcomes.low: Push for more details than she's comfortable giving, or dismiss it as unimportant

events.notes: Plants the narrative seed for the Day 30 exchange/ending twist. Should fire at least once before day 25 if possible.

events.title: Shiori Wants to Talk
events.description: Shiori asks to grab coffee, just the two of you. She's not being dramatic about it, but it's clear she wants to talk about how things are going with Hiyori.
events.player_action_prompt: Shiori wants an honest conversation about what's going on with Hiyori. What do you tell her?

affection_outcomes.high: Be honest about your feelings without oversharing details that aren't yours to share
affection_outcomes.mid: Give a vague, deflective answer
affection_outcomes.low: Overshare inappropriately or dismiss her concern

events.notes: Whatever the player tells Shiori here becomes part of Shiori's knowledge base going forward. Shiori-focused, but scores against Hiyori's meter (no `affects` field): Shiori has no meter of her own and isn't a route. She's protective of Hiyori, so how Adrian treats her reaches Hiyori indirectly.

events.title: Inter-Hall Sports Tournament
events.description: Adrian's hall is short-handed for the inter-hall tournament, and Hiyori's cycling club has been sharing the sports hall for training all week. The two groups end up doing warm-ups together more days than not.
events.player_action_prompt: Training's about to start and Hiyori's group is stretching two mats over. What do you do?

affection_outcomes.high: Strike up an easy, low-pressure conversation without making it a big deal
affection_outcomes.mid: Nod and keep to your own group
affection_outcomes.low: Awkwardly avoid eye contact or make it weird

events.notes: Active event. Deliberately low-affection-accessible and physical/energetic — a tonal break from the academic-flavored arcs.

sub_events.description: A stray ball from Adrian's side nearly takes Hiyori out mid-drill. She's fine, just glaring at whoever threw it.
sub_events.player_action_prompt: She's looking right at you, probably assuming it was your team's fault. What do you do?

affection_outcomes.high: Own it, apologize properly, offer to grab her water bottle or whatever rolled away
affection_outcomes.mid: Apologize on behalf of the team and move on
affection_outcomes.low: Deflect blame or laugh it off without actually apologizing

sub_events.description: Tournament day. Hiyori's cycling club is there supporting a different event, but she swings by Adrian's match for a bit between her own commitments.
sub_events.player_action_prompt: You spot her in the small crowd during a break. Do you acknowledge it?

affection_outcomes.high: Give her a quick wave or nod between plays, stay focused otherwise
affection_outcomes.mid: Notice her but don't do anything about it
affection_outcomes.low: Get distracted enough that it visibly affects your game

sub_events.description: Shared training slot again. Your hall on one half of the court, her cycling club stretching on the other.
sub_events.player_action_prompt: You're both in the same space with time before things start properly. What do you do?

affection_outcomes.high: Easy conversation, no agenda — treat it as normal
affection_outcomes.mid: Stick with your own group
affection_outcomes.low: Try too hard to get her attention

sub_events.description: Post-training evening outside the sports hall — everyone's aching, sprawled on the steps arguing about tomorrow's lineup. Her club's packing up nearby.
sub_events.player_action_prompt: It's loose, low-stakes downtime and she's around. How do you play it?

affection_outcomes.high: Include her naturally without singling her out
affection_outcomes.mid: Stay in your own conversation
affection_outcomes.low: Make a show of noticing her

events.title: The Cycling Trip
events.description: What started as Hiyori's offhand cycling club invite turns into an actual weekend trip along the park connectors — further and longer than the usual 'easy beginner route' framing suggested.
events.player_action_prompt: The group's spread out further than expected and you end up riding near the back with just Hiyori. What's the conversation like?

affection_outcomes.high: Easy, unforced conversation — let comfortable silences happen too
affection_outcomes.mid: Small talk, nothing memorable either way
affection_outcomes.low: Force conversation or make her feel like she has to entertain you

events.notes: Active event. Natural escalation of hiyori_cycling_invite. Short duration — uses the plain probability/force-out mechanic, no locked final-day sub-event.

sub_events.description: The group takes a wrong turn and splits up without meaning to. It's just you and Hiyori for a while, trying to find the right path back.
sub_events.player_action_prompt: You're both a little lost and losing daylight. How do you handle it?

affection_outcomes.high: Stay calm, make it into something to laugh about rather than stress over
affection_outcomes.mid: Focus on just fixing the problem, minimal conversation
affection_outcomes.low: Get visibly stressed or blame her for the wrong turn

sub_events.description: The group stops to rest at a scenic point along the route. Everyone's spread out; you end up sitting near Hiyori while she catches her breath.
sub_events.player_action_prompt: It's quiet, and neither of you has said anything for a bit. Do you break the silence?

affection_outcomes.high: Say something genuine, not performative, about the ride or the view
affection_outcomes.mid: Stay comfortably quiet without it feeling awkward
affection_outcomes.low: Fill the silence with something forced or off-topic

sub_events.description: A long flat stretch of the route. The group's strung out and conversation comes and goes with the pace.
sub_events.player_action_prompt: You're riding near her for a while with nothing particular to say. What do you do?

affection_outcomes.high: Let it be easy — talk when there's something to say, don't force it
affection_outcomes.mid: Keep to small talk
affection_outcomes.low: Fill every silence or try to impress her with your pace

sub_events.description: Evening after a long day of riding. Everyone's sunburnt, sore, and too tired to be self-conscious.
sub_events.player_action_prompt: The group's winding down and she's nearby. What do you do?

affection_outcomes.high: Be good company without needing it to go anywhere
affection_outcomes.mid: Keep to yourself, you're tired too
affection_outcomes.low: Push for a moment alone when she's clearly exhausted

events.title: Yuki's Case Competition
events.description: The 'help me with a basic stats concept' favor turns out to be prep for an actual econs case competition Yuki's entering. She won't admit she's nervous about it, but she keeps texting to schedule 'just one more session.'
events.player_action_prompt: Yuki's laid out her notes but hasn't actually started explaining anything yet — she's stalling. What do you do?

affection_outcomes.high: Let her set the pace, don't push, just be present
affection_outcomes.mid: Get straight to the material
affection_outcomes.low: Call out that she's stalling in a way that puts her on the spot

events.notes: Yuki's route arc — gated on yuki_affection rather than the main Hiyori-affection meter (new field: yuki_affection_required), matching her route's stage-gated, attention-driven design. First extended arc for her route; previously only single-scene secret_end_events existed.

sub_events.description: A study session runs later than planned. Yuki doesn't seem in a hurry to end it, even after the material's covered.
sub_events.player_action_prompt: The actual studying wrapped up a while ago but neither of you has moved to leave. What do you do?

affection_outcomes.high: Let the conversation drift somewhere more personal, follow her lead
affection_outcomes.mid: Wrap up efficiently and head out
affection_outcomes.low: Make it awkward by pointing out you're both just sitting there

sub_events.description: Competition day. Yuki's visibly more nervous than she's let on all week. She finds you beforehand, ostensibly to return a borrowed textbook.
sub_events.player_action_prompt: She's clearly not really here about the textbook. What do you say?

affection_outcomes.high: Say something that actually settles her nerves, without making a big deal of it
affection_outcomes.mid: Wish her luck and let her go
affection_outcomes.low: Miss that she's nervous entirely, or make a joke that lands wrong

sub_events.description: Another prep block with Yuki — practice cases, a whiteboard, her handwriting getting messier as she goes.
sub_events.player_action_prompt: She's grinding through material she half-understands. How do you help?

affection_outcomes.high: Work at her pace and let her get things wrong without judgment
affection_outcomes.mid: Explain it correctly and move on
affection_outcomes.low: Get impatient or make her feel slow

sub_events.description: Evening messages from Yuki — a question about a model, then another, then one that isn't really about the model.
sub_events.player_action_prompt: The questions have drifted away from econs. What do you do?

affection_outcomes.high: Follow where she's actually going without calling it out
affection_outcomes.mid: Answer what was literally asked
affection_outcomes.low: Shut the conversation down once the studying's technically done

events.title: Finals Week
events.description: Finals season hits everyone at once. The library run-ins with Hiyori stop being occasional and start being nightly — same floor, same corner, same collective exhaustion.
events.player_action_prompt: You've both been at the library for hours and it's clear neither of you is retaining anything anymore. What do you do?

affection_outcomes.high: Suggest an actual break — food, fresh air, something that isn't studying
affection_outcomes.mid: Keep grinding separately, minimal interaction
affection_outcomes.low: Vent your own stress at her or make the mood worse

events.notes: Active event. Escalates library_late_night into a sustained arc. Timed for late in the 30-day window, thematically tied to end-of-semester.

sub_events.description: Hiyori finally cracks a little — not dramatically, just a tired, honest moment about how much this semester's been wearing her down.
sub_events.player_action_prompt: She's said more than she probably meant to. How do you respond?

affection_outcomes.high: Actually listen, don't immediately try to fix or minimize it
affection_outcomes.mid: Offer a generic reassurance and move on
affection_outcomes.low: Change the subject or make it about your own stress instead

sub_events.description: One of the harder papers just ended. Everyone's drained. Someone suggests food — somehow it ends up being just you and Hiyori who actually go.
sub_events.player_action_prompt: First real meal either of you has had that isn't instant noodles in days. What's the vibe?

affection_outcomes.high: Relaxed, a little giddy from the exam being over — let that show
affection_outcomes.mid: Pleasant but low-energy, both too tired for much
affection_outcomes.low: Immediately start stressing about the next paper instead of enjoying the moment

sub_events.description: The last paper. You run into Hiyori right as she's walking out of the hall, visibly relieved it's over.
sub_events.player_action_prompt: It's officially done. What do you say to her?

affection_outcomes.high: Something genuine about getting through the semester, not just a generic 'good job'
affection_outcomes.mid: A quick, low-effort congratulations
affection_outcomes.low: Immediately pivot to your own results/stress instead of hers

sub_events.description: Daytime revision. Same study space, same exhausted faces, Hiyori a few seats over with a highlighter she isn't really using.
sub_events.player_action_prompt: You're both running on fumes in the same room. What do you do?

affection_outcomes.high: Small, practical kindness — coffee, a saved seat, no big gestures
affection_outcomes.mid: Focus on your own revision
affection_outcomes.low: Interrupt her focus to talk

sub_events.description: The library at night during finals. Half the campus is here and nobody's leaving.
sub_events.player_action_prompt: It's late and neither of you has moved in hours. How do you handle it?

affection_outcomes.high: Notice when she's hit her limit and suggest stopping
affection_outcomes.mid: Keep grinding in parallel
affection_outcomes.low: Make the mood worse by spiralling out loud

events.title: The Exchange Decision
events.description: The exchange program Hiyori mentioned 'on a whim' turns out to be very real — she's gotten in, and now has to actually decide whether to go. She's not telling most people yet.
events.player_action_prompt: Hiyori tells you about the offer before she's told almost anyone else. Why do you think she's telling you?

affection_outcomes.high: Ask what she actually wants, not what she thinks she should do
affection_outcomes.mid: Listen without pushing either way
affection_outcomes.low: Make it about how it affects you instead of supporting her decision

events.notes: Pays off the exchange_rumor thread planted earlier — per README's design principle, this late-game twist should feel earned, not arbitrary. Highest-stakes extended event; recommend prioritizing this one first if only writing a subset for now.

sub_events.description: Hiyori's clearly been going back and forth on this for days. She brings it up again, unprompted, like she's still trying to talk herself into a decision.
sub_events.player_action_prompt: She's thinking out loud more than actually asking for input. What do you do?

affection_outcomes.high: Ask good questions instead of giving your opinion outright
affection_outcomes.mid: Give a neutral, safe response
affection_outcomes.low: Push your own preference onto her decision

sub_events.description: Hiyori's made her decision. She tells you before anyone else finds out.
sub_events.player_action_prompt: This is a real moment for her, whichever way it went. How do you react?

affection_outcomes.high: Be genuinely present for her, whatever she decided, without making it about your own feelings on the matter
affection_outcomes.mid: Acknowledge it and move on
affection_outcomes.low: React in a way that's clearly about how it affects you

sub_events.description: Normal day, except it isn't. She hasn't brought the exchange up again and neither have you, but it's sitting there.
sub_events.player_action_prompt: She's acting like everything's normal. Do you leave it alone?

affection_outcomes.high: Let her raise it in her own time, stay easy to talk to
affection_outcomes.mid: Keep things normal and say nothing
affection_outcomes.low: Keep steering the conversation back to it

sub_events.description: A late message from Hiyori about something unrelated. It's clearly not what she's actually thinking about.
sub_events.player_action_prompt: She's texting about nothing at midnight. What do you do?

affection_outcomes.high: Stay up and talk about nothing for as long as she needs to
affection_outcomes.mid: Reply briefly and turn in
affection_outcomes.low: Press her about the decision directly

events.title: Shiori's Interview Crunch
events.description: Shiori's got a CS internship interview coming up and, uncharacteristically, actually asks Adrian for help prepping — usually she's the one giving advice, not asking for it.
events.player_action_prompt: Shiori's running through a practice answer and it's clearly not landing, even to her. What do you do?

affection_outcomes.high: Give honest, specific feedback rather than just reassurance
affection_outcomes.mid: Offer generic encouragement
affection_outcomes.low: Brush off the mock interview as not a big deal

events.notes: Not a Hiyori-focused arc — deepens Adrian's friendship with Shiori directly, and gives her a moment of vulnerability outside her usual protective/advisory role. Shiori-focused, but scores against Hiyori's meter (no `affects` field): Shiori has no meter of her own and isn't a route. She's protective of Hiyori, so how Adrian treats her reaches Hiyori indirectly.

sub_events.description: Mid-prep, Shiori admits — almost like it slips out — that she's more nervous about this than she's letting on.
sub_events.player_action_prompt: This isn't the version of Shiori you usually see. What do you do?

affection_outcomes.high: Take it seriously instead of brushing past it
affection_outcomes.mid: Acknowledge it briefly and get back to prep
affection_outcomes.low: Make a joke that undercuts the moment

sub_events.description: Interview day. Shiori texts you right after — she wants to know your read before she even tells you how it went.
sub_events.player_action_prompt: She's asking what you think before revealing anything herself. What do you say?

affection_outcomes.high: Be genuinely encouraging based on the actual prep work, not just empty positivity
affection_outcomes.mid: Give a brief, generic 'I'm sure it went fine'
affection_outcomes.low: Deflect or seem uninterested in the outcome

sub_events.description: Another mock round. Shiori's answers are getting tighter but she's still second-guessing every one of them.
sub_events.player_action_prompt: She wants feedback and she can tell when you're softening it. What do you give her?

affection_outcomes.high: Honest, specific notes — she asked for real help, not comfort
affection_outcomes.mid: Mostly encouragement, light on specifics
affection_outcomes.low: Nitpick in a way that rattles her confidence

sub_events.description: Late-night messages from Shiori — a question about a data structure, then one about whether she's wasting everyone's time.
sub_events.player_action_prompt: The self-doubt just leaked through. How do you respond?

affection_outcomes.high: Take it seriously and remind her what she's actually good at
affection_outcomes.mid: Answer the technical question and let the rest slide
affection_outcomes.low: Brush the doubt off with a joke

events.title: Hiyori's Tutoring Gig
events.description: Hiyori tutors secondary schoolers on the side — something she doesn't really advertise. Adrian ends up helping her prep materials for an upcoming open house session.
events.player_action_prompt: You're watching Hiyori explain a concept to a whiteboard mock-up, completely different register than how she normally talks to you. What do you do?

affection_outcomes.high: Notice and genuinely appreciate this side of her without making it weird
affection_outcomes.mid: Help with the practical prep work without commenting on it
affection_outcomes.low: Tease her about it in a way that makes her clam up

events.notes: Shows Hiyori in caretaker mode — a real change of register from her usual tsundere deflection with Adrian specifically.

sub_events.description: Late prep session, surrounded by worksheets and practice problems. Hiyori's noticeably more relaxed talking about teaching than she usually is talking about herself.
sub_events.player_action_prompt: She's in her element here in a way you don't usually see. Do you say anything about it?

affection_outcomes.high: Point it out gently, in a way that's clearly a compliment, not a callout
affection_outcomes.mid: Stay focused on the task without commenting
affection_outcomes.low: Make an offhand comment that embarrasses her out of it

sub_events.description: Open house day. Hiyori's clearly good at this — patient, clear, the secondary schoolers actually like her. She catches you watching afterward.
sub_events.player_action_prompt: She just caught you watching her teach. What do you say?

affection_outcomes.high: Say something specific and genuine about what you noticed, not generic praise
affection_outcomes.mid: Give a brief compliment and move on
affection_outcomes.low: Deflect or act like you weren't paying attention

sub_events.description: Worksheets, practice papers, printing that goes wrong twice. Hiyori's particular about how the material's laid out.
sub_events.player_action_prompt: It's fiddly prep work and she cares about it more than she lets on. How do you help?

affection_outcomes.high: Take her standards seriously and do it properly
affection_outcomes.mid: Do the tasks you're given
affection_outcomes.low: Rush it or tease her for caring so much

sub_events.description: Evening spent marking practice scripts. She keeps writing full explanations in the margins for kids who probably won't read them.
sub_events.player_action_prompt: She's putting far more in than the job asks for. Do you say anything?

affection_outcomes.high: Notice it out loud, warmly, without making her defensive
affection_outcomes.mid: Keep marking, say nothing
affection_outcomes.low: Point out she's wasting her time

events.title: Hall Camp Weekend
events.description: An overnight hall camp — the usual mix of forced team games, a campfire, and too many people crammed into too little space. Hiyori's there as a guest of a friend in the hall.
events.player_action_prompt: A game puts you and Hiyori on the same team, working closer together than either of you probably planned for.

affection_outcomes.high: Play it easy and collaborative, let the forced proximity actually be fun
affection_outcomes.mid: Go through the motions without much energy
affection_outcomes.low: Make the pairing awkward by overthinking it visibly

events.notes: Active event. Leans more directly into romantic-tension energy than most of the other arcs. Short duration — plain probability/force-out mechanic, no locked final-day sub-event.

sub_events.description: Campfire night. The group's thinned out as people wander off to sleep, and somehow you and Hiyori end up as two of the last few still sitting there.
sub_events.player_action_prompt: It's quiet except for the fire. What do you do?

affection_outcomes.high: Let the conversation go somewhere more real than the earlier group banter
affection_outcomes.mid: Keep things light, stick to safe topics
affection_outcomes.low: Force the moment into something it isn't

sub_events.description: Everyone's exhausted and unglamorous the morning after — bad sleep, messy hair, no one at their best. Hiyori included.
sub_events.player_action_prompt: She looks a little self-conscious about how she looks right now. What do you do?

affection_outcomes.high: Act completely normal about it, don't make it a thing
affection_outcomes.mid: Don't acknowledge it either way
affection_outcomes.low: Comment on it in a way that makes her more self-conscious

sub_events.description: Station games in the sun. Forced enthusiasm, questionable rules, everyone slightly damp.
sub_events.player_action_prompt: The games keep throwing your group together. How do you play it?

affection_outcomes.high: Commit to the silliness — it's easier to be around you when you're not overthinking
affection_outcomes.mid: Participate without much energy
affection_outcomes.low: Opt out and make the group work around you

sub_events.description: Night activities running late — someone's guitar, someone's bad ghost story, people drifting between groups.
sub_events.player_action_prompt: It's loose and unstructured and she's somewhere in the mix. What do you do?

affection_outcomes.high: Be around without engineering a moment
affection_outcomes.mid: Stay with whoever you're already talking to
affection_outcomes.low: Hover at the edge of whatever group she's in, waiting for an opening

events.title: When She's Sick
events.description: What started as Hiyori going quiet in the group chat turns into an actual multi-day flu. Shiori's been checking on her, but she can't always be there.
events.player_action_prompt: Shiori mentions she can't check on Hiyori today — exam clash. Someone should probably bring her something to eat.

affection_outcomes.high: Offer to go yourself without making it a whole production
affection_outcomes.mid: Ask Shiori to sort it out instead of stepping up yourself
affection_outcomes.low: Don't offer at all

events.notes: Escalates hiyori_sick into a sustained caretaking arc — quieter and more emotionally intimate than most of the others, without needing an external plot device.

sub_events.description: Hiyori answers the door looking rough — not her usual composed self at all — and is clearly caught off guard that you actually showed up.
sub_events.player_action_prompt: She's letting her guard down more than usual just because she's too tired to keep it up. What do you do?

affection_outcomes.high: Keep it low-key and practical — don't make her perform being okay for you
affection_outcomes.mid: Drop off the food and don't stay long
affection_outcomes.low: Make her feel like she has to entertain you despite being sick

sub_events.description: Hiyori's back to normal, more or less, and immediately tries to downplay the whole thing when she sees you.
sub_events.player_action_prompt: She's clearly trying to act like it wasn't a big deal. Do you let her?

affection_outcomes.high: Let her downplay it if she wants, but make clear you're glad she's okay
affection_outcomes.mid: Go along with the downplaying completely
affection_outcomes.low: Push the point and embarrass her about needing help

sub_events.description: She's still in her room. Shiori's relaying updates, and the group chat's gone quiet out of politeness.
sub_events.player_action_prompt: You don't want to crowd her but you'd like to know she's okay. What do you do?

affection_outcomes.high: One low-pressure message that doesn't demand a reply
affection_outcomes.mid: Wait for Shiori's next update
affection_outcomes.low: Message repeatedly until she answers

sub_events.description: A short reply from Hiyori at night — mostly fine, mostly lying, definitely still ill.
sub_events.player_action_prompt: She's downplaying how rough it is. How do you respond?

affection_outcomes.high: Let her downplay it, but make it easy to ask for something if she needs it
affection_outcomes.mid: Take the 'I'm fine' at face value
affection_outcomes.low: Argue with her about how sick she actually is

events.title: The Other Guy
events.description: The guy who asked Hiyori out doesn't take the 'let me think about it' as a no. He keeps showing up — coincidentally, allegedly — over the next few days.
events.player_action_prompt: You spot him talking to Hiyori again, and this is the third time this week. What do you do?

affection_outcomes.high: Stay calm and let Hiyori handle it herself, be there if she wants to talk after
affection_outcomes.mid: Notice it but don't do anything
affection_outcomes.low: Get visibly jealous or possessive about it

events.notes: The one arc built explicitly around jealousy/rivalry — gives the player real agency in how to handle it rather than just reacting to something happening to Hiyori.

sub_events.description: Hiyori brings it up herself, a little frustrated — he's not being pushy exactly, just persistent in a way she doesn't know how to shut down without being harsh.
sub_events.player_action_prompt: She's asking, in a roundabout way, what you think she should do. How do you respond?

affection_outcomes.high: Support whatever she decides without pushing your own stake in it
affection_outcomes.mid: Give a neutral, uninvested answer
affection_outcomes.low: Make it obvious you want her to reject him, for your own reasons

sub_events.description: Hiyori finally gives him a clear answer. She tells you about it after, watching your reaction more closely than she'd probably admit.
sub_events.player_action_prompt: She's telling you how it went and clearly gauging your reaction. What do you do?

affection_outcomes.high: React genuinely but without making it about your own feelings for her
affection_outcomes.mid: Acknowledge it briefly and move on
affection_outcomes.low: Overreact in a way that makes your own feelings obvious and puts her on the spot

sub_events.description: He's around again — canteen, corridor, walking the same direction she is. Nothing you could point at, exactly.
sub_events.player_action_prompt: You keep noticing. What do you actually do about it?

affection_outcomes.high: Nothing. It's hers to handle, and you don't make it her problem to manage you
affection_outcomes.mid: Notice it and move on
affection_outcomes.low: Insert yourself into the conversation

sub_events.description: Night, phone in hand, rereading a message from Hiyori that has nothing to do with him.
sub_events.player_action_prompt: You're spiralling a bit. What do you send?

affection_outcomes.high: Reply to what she actually said, and leave it at that
affection_outcomes.mid: Leave it until morning
affection_outcomes.low: Fish for information about him

good_end.title: She Said Yes
good_end.description: You find the moment. Maybe it's after the cultural show, maybe it's a quiet evening walk back from the library. You say it. She looks away first — classic — and then back at you. 'I was wondering when you'd say something,' she says, and she's smiling.
good_end.scene: End scene: the two of you walking along the canal near UTown at dusk. She's cycling slowly beside you. The city is doing its thing. It's quiet in the right way.

friend_zone_end.title: I Think of You as a Friend
friend_zone_end.description: She's kind about it. That's almost worse. 'I really like you as a person, Adrian,' she says. 'I just — I don't think I feel that way.' She means it. She hopes you'll still be friends. She's not sure you will be. Neither are you.
friend_zone_end.scene: You walk back to your hostel alone. The city is the same as always. You are slightly different.

bad_end.title: Please Don't
bad_end.trigger: confess with affection below 40, or multiple wrong moves accumulate
bad_end.description: She's uncomfortable. You can see it. She keeps it civil — she's not cruel — but there's a distance in her eyes that wasn't there before. She excuses herself. Shiori finds out. Things are awkward for a while.
bad_end.scene: You see her at the Science canteen a week later. She's with Shiori. They're laughing about something. She glances over, briefly, and looks away first.

too_late_end.title: Too Late
too_late_end.description: Out of nowhere, Hiyori announces she's been accepted into an overseas exchange program starting next semester, followed by a year-long internship abroad. It happened fast — faster than she expected too. You never said anything, and now the timing has closed the door on its own.
too_late_end.scene: You run into her near the bus stop with her luggage, heading to the airport shuttle. 'See you in two years, I guess,' she says, half-joking. She means it as a joke. Neither of you laughs quite right.

secret_end.title: It Was Always You
secret_end.trigger: Yuki's hidden affection >= 70, player never triggered main confession with Hiyori
secret_end.description: It's late. You're walking back from the library with Yuki — this has been happening more and more lately, without either of you really planning it. She stops walking. 'Can I tell you something?' she says. 'And you can't make it weird.' She takes a breath. 'I think I've liked you for a really long time. Since secondary school, maybe. I just — I thought you knew, and then I thought you didn't, and then I gave up. But I don't want to give up anymore.'
secret_end.scene: The two of you sit on a bench outside the library for another hour just talking. About secondary school. About now. About what this means. It's not dramatic. It's just honest. That's all it ever needed to be.
